pageTitle: Triviacon — Run the quiz night, not the tech
pageDescription: A free, portable desktop app for hosting live trivia nights. One laptop, two screens, no install, no account, fully offline. Windows, Linux, macOS.
ogDescription: Free, portable trivia host. One laptop, two screens, fully offline.
pillText: is out — read the release notes
heroTitle:
Run the quiz night.
Not the tech.
heroLede: Triviacon turns one laptop into a two-screen trivia show: you drive from the control panel, the room watches the game screen on a projector or TV.
stageAria: Control panel and game screen side by side
altGame: Game screen shown to the audience
featTitle: Everything a quiz night needs. Nothing it doesn't.
featLede: Built by a quiz host, playtested in real rooms with real projectors and bad WiFi.
f1b: The control panel stays on your laptop with answers, notes and scores. The game screen goes to the projector and shows only what you reveal — when you reveal it.
f2b: Single answer, multiple choice and list — with rich-text formatting.
f3b: Attach media to the question and a second slot revealed with the answer. Audio-only mode hides a video that would give it away.
f4b: Live scoring with half points, a staged podium reveal and tiebreakers that settle it fairly.
f5b: Per-question countdown, plus notes only you can see.
f6b: A .tcq bundles questions and media. Share it, back it up, open it anywhere. Crash-safe saving.
f7b: Ten built-in control-panel themes and a custom splash screen with artwork and music. Ships in English and Polish — and a new language is just one more locale file.
tourTitle: What you see. What they see.
tourLede: Pick a phase — jump between them freely during a live game.
note_board: The panel lists every question with its answer; the audience sees only which ones are still in play.
note_question: Media plays on the game screen. Here the video is in audio-only mode, so a visualizer stands in for the picture.
note_ranking: Reveal the standings place by place. Ties on the podium go to a tiebreaker.
note_builder: Categories on the left, questions in the middle, media and answers on the right. The game screen stays dark while you build.
howTitle: From empty file to final podium
s1b: Add categories, questions and media in the Builder — or open someone's .tcq.
s2b: Type in the teams and press Start when everyone's seated.
s3b: One click, then drag it to the projector or second display.
s4b: Reveal questions and answers, award points, and close with the podium.
is1: One machine, two screens — a host panel and an audience display
is2: Portable — no install, runs from a USB stick, fully offline
is3: Yours to run — you score, you navigate, you make the calls
is4: Self-contained quiz files you own and share
is5: AI helps build and present — you write the quiz
isnt1: Online — nothing to fail in a room with bad WiFi
isnt2: An account — no sign-up, no cloud, nothing tracked
isnt3: An auto-scorer — trivia runs on human judgment
isnt4: A fixed track — jump between phases whenever you like
isnt5: A quiz writer — the questions, difficulty and media are yours
quote: “The car to a bicycle — but it never drives itself.”
dlLede: No installer, no admin rights. Settings live next to the app, so it leaves nothing behind.
releaseFail: Buttons open the GitHub releases page.
demoBody: Open it in Triviacon and click through a full game — every media type the app supports, including audio-only video. AI-generated media, free to redistribute.
q1: Do players need phones or an app?
a1: No. Teams answer on paper or out loud — the room just watches the game screen. You score by hand.
a2: Never. Everything, media included, lives in the .tcq file on your machine.
q3: Will macOS or Windows warn me when I open it?
a3: Possibly — the builds aren't code-signed yet. On macOS, right-click the app and choose Open the first time.
a4: Yes — a language is one JSON locale file. Contributions are welcome on GitHub.
